mcq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{When solving the wave equation by separation of variables, we assume the solution has the form:}\)
\(\text{Substituting } y(x,t)=X(x)T(t) \text{ into the wave equation } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2}=c^2\frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2} \text{ leads to:}\)
\(\text{For the vibrating string problem, which case of the separation constant } k\\ \text{ yields the physically appropriate periodic solution?}\)
\(\text{When } k<0 \text{ (say } k=-\lambda^2), \text{ the solution for } X(x) \text{ is:}\)

\(\text{For the vibrating string fixed at } x=0 \text{ and } x=l, \text{ applying } y(0,t)=0 \text{ to the solution }\\ y=(A\cos\lambda x+B\sin\lambda x)(C\cos\lambda ct+D\sin\lambda ct) \text{ gives:}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Wave equation: } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{1. String is homogeneous and perfectly elastic.}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{2. Tension is large; gravity negligible.}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{3. Transverse vibrations are small (small slope).}\)

(2 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{State the one-dimensional wave equation for a vibrating string and list the physical assumptions made in its derivation.}\)

sq.ANSWER:
Upto the stepMarks

\(\text{Let } y(x,t)=X(x)T(t). \text{ Substituting gives } XT''=c^2 X''T.\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Separate: } \frac{X''}{X} = \frac{T''}{c^2 T} = k \text{ (constant).}\)

(2 Mark)

\(\text{Case 1: } k>0, k=\lambda^2: X''-\lambda^2 X=0, T''-\lambda^2 c^2 T=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Case 2: } k<0, k=-\lambda^2: X''+\lambda^2 X=0, T''+\lambda^2 c^2 T=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{Case 3: } k=0: X''=0, T''=0.\)

(1 Mark)

\(\text{The solutions for each case are exponential, trigonometric, or linear.}\)

(1 Mark)
sq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Using separation of variables, solve } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2} \text{ and obtain the ODEs for } X(x) \text{ and } T(t). \text{ Discuss the three cases for the separation constant.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Assume \(y(x,t)=X(x)T(t)\). Substitute into PDE to get \(XT'' = c^2X''T\).}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Separate variables: \(\dfrac{X''}{X} = \dfrac{T''}{(c^2T)} = k\) (constant).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Case \(k > 0\) (\(k=\lambda^2\)): \(X'' - \lambda^2X=0\), \(T'' - \lambda^2c^2T=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) solutions: \(X = Ae^{\lambda x}+Be^{-\lambda x}\), \(T = Ce^{\lambda ct}+De^{-\lambda ct}\).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Case \(k < 0\) (\(k=-\lambda^2\)): \(X'' + \lambda^2X=0\), \(T'' + \lambda^2c^2T=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) solutions: \(X = A \cos(\lambda x) + B \sin(\lambda x)\), \(T = C \cos(\lambda c t) + D \sin(\lambda c t)\).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Case \(k = 0\): \(X''=0\), \(T''=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(X = Ax+B\), \(T = Ct+D\).}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{For vibrating string with fixed ends, boundary conditions \(y(0,t)=0\), \(y(l,t)=0\) require periodic solutions in space.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Trigonometric solutions (sine and cosine) are periodic and satisfy fixed end conditions naturally after applying BCs.}\) (2 Marks)
Exponential and linear solutions do not represent bounded vibrations for a finite string. (2 Marks)
Hence trigonometric form is suitable. (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Using separation of variables, derive the three possible solutions of the one-dimensional}\\ \text{wave equation } \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2}.\\ \text{Explain why the trigonometric solution is most suitable for a vibrating string problem with fixed ends.}\)

lq.ANSWER:
Step Marks
\(\text{Assume \(y(x,t)=X(x)T(t)\). Separate to get \(\dfrac{X''}{X} = \dfrac{T''}{(c^2T) }= k\)}.\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{For vibrating string, choose \(k = -\lambda^2\) (negative for oscillatory solutions).}\) (1 Mark)
\(\text{Solve \(X'' + \lambda^2X = 0\) with \(X(0)=0\), \(X(l)=0\).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Get \(X(x) = B \sin(\lambda x)\). Apply \(X(l)=0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\sin(\lambda l) = 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(\lambda = \dfrac{n\pi}{l}\), \(n=1,2,3,\ldots\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Solve \(T'' + \lambda^2c^2T = 0\) \(\Rightarrow\) \(T(t) = C \cos(\lambda c t) + D \sin(\lambda c t)\).}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Thus solution for each \(n\): \(y_n(x,t) = \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right) + D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{General solution: \(y(x,t) = \sum\limits_{n=1}^{\infty} \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi x}{l}\right)\left[C_n \cos\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right) + D_n \sin\left(\dfrac{n\pi c t}{l}\right)\right].\)}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Natural frequencies: \(\omega_n = \dfrac{n\pi c}{l}\) (rad/s) or \(f_n = \dfrac{nc}{2l}\) Hz.}\) (2 Marks)
\(\text{Interpretation: \(n=1\) fundamental mode, higher \(n\) are overtones.}\) (1 Mark)
lq.QUESTION_DESC: \(\text{Solve the one-dimensional wave equation \( \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial t^2} = c^2 \frac{\partial^2 y}{\partial x^2} \text{ by separation of variables}\)}\\ \text{subject to the boundary conditions \( y(0,t)=0, y(l,t)=0 \text{ for all } t\geq 0.\)}\\ \text{Obtain the general solution in the form of a series and identify the natural frequencies of vibration.}\)
